priorActualFailure.observed: The actual old run reported one failure at the first PLAY condition after the NEW GAME action; the log directly records the timeout and its original source location. No newer iOS execution is represented here.
priorActualFailure.hypothesis: The old action coordinates were DOM viewport values sent to native /actions without calibrated translation. This is a source-supported possible cause, not a confirmed diagnosis from a repaired native tap.
priorActualFailure.sourceBasis: The pinned v12.1.3 performActions implementation forwards coordinates to WDA without translating them and removes duration-zero pause actions. The public calibration method visits its own calibration page and restores the previous URL on success.

measured: The exact acquisition script was run at stubbed HTTP/WebDriver/filesystem/clock boundaries through the original first-PLAY-timeout path. It retains nine passing prechecks supplied by the fixture, one original failure, calibration and both CSS/native actions.

Calibration executes before instrumentation and device/title measurements, and waits for the reloaded application ready state. Source reading locates only two calibration calls: before NEW GAME and after refresh before CONTINUE, outside active play.

The exact report JSON printed to the ordinary job-log boundary equals the saved report. A 68-byte PNG fixture round-trips with matching byte count and SHA256; payload chunks obey the 4000-character limit.

When failure-state, screenshot and session cleanup boundaries all throw, all three diagnostic errors are recorded while the original PLAY timeout remains the primary failure and the report is saved/printed.

An image exceeding 1500000 bytes remains at the file boundary and is skipped by log serialization without losing the report. A missing-UDID failure writes/prints its report without any HTTP/WebDriver/server call.

Independent numeric checks execute the pinned calibrated driver branch. The helper follows its OR scaling condition and applies endpoint integer rounding; invalid calibration/viewport/origin inputs fail before dispatch and frozen input actions remain unchanged.

Independent execution of the pinned driver preprocessing retains all eight positive-pause ticks. Both bounded timeline interpretations contain positive two-contact overlap. Actual WDA timing remains unmeasured.

The exact event recorder and trust predicates reject misplaced/wrong-type/untrusted title events and sequential, duplicate-ID, canceled, untrusted or mouse-only contact traces. All trust values in these tests are explicit fixture values, not native events.
limitations: No local browser, local server, socket, Appium, Simulator, credentials or permission changes were used. The stubbed acquisition script is not an actual browser test.

The public calibration data rounds offsets; the internal driver retains floating values. The helper follows the public data and additionally rounds action endpoints. It is not asserted to be bit-identical to internal floating output.

Actual Safari chrome geometry, calibration reliability/reload timing, native touch placement and overlap, game movement/attack effects, orientation restoration and persistence still require the new real CI.
The CPU failure probe intentionally ends at the first PLAY timeout; it does not execute the complete game gate. The second calibration call is verified by source order only.

Filesystem availability and GitHub log delivery/truncation are not tested by the in-memory boundary. The report/PNG checks establish script serialization fidelity, not external retrieval success. Oversized images remain artifact-only and are not replaced by the smaller fixture.
The parent and refuter each encountered a CPU-wrapper setup syntax error, fixed only in their diagnostic harnesses. Separate setup records are retained; neither is a product or iOS finding.
Earlier dialogue and iOS evidence is preserved. This PASS does not promote the failed old run, satisfy a quality element or replace the required blind comparison.
